+import os

+import subprocess
+import sys

+
+
+class DevelopmentProcessRobotTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Run the production Robot check with the built RCC in isolated Git repos."""
+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.repo_root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+        binary_override = os.environ.get("RCC_ACCEPTANCE_BINARY")
+        cls.binary = (
+            Path(binary_override).expanduser().resolve()
+            if binary_override
+            else cls.repo_root / "build" / ("rcc.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "rcc")
+        )
+        if not cls.binary.is_file() or not os.access(cls.binary, os.X_OK):
+            raise AssertionError(f"RCC_ACCEPTANCE_BINARY must name an executable file: {cls.binary}")
+        cls.robot_dir = cls.repo_root / "robot_tests"
+        cls.rcc_version = subprocess.run(
+            [str(cls.binary), "--version"],
+            check=True,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        ).stdout.strip()
+        if not cls.rcc_version or "\n" in cls.rcc_version or "\r" in cls.rcc_version:
+            raise AssertionError(f"built RCC reported an invalid version: {cls.rcc_version!r}")
+
+    def test_accepts_regular_changelog_commit(self):
+        self._assert_robot_result("normal", should_pass=True)
+
+    def test_accepts_merge_when_current_changelog_is_tracked_in_tree(self):
+        self._assert_robot_result("merge", should_pass=True)
+
+    def test_rejects_missing_tracked_changelog(self):
+        self._assert_robot_result("missing", should_pass=False)
+
+    def test_rejects_untracked_matching_changelog(self):
+        self._assert_robot_result("untracked", should_pass=False)
+
+    def test_rejects_wrong_version_heading(self):
+        self._assert_robot_result("wrong-version", should_pass=False)
+
+    def _assert_robot_result(self, layout, should_pass):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="rcc-development-process-") as temp:
+            fixture = Path(temp)
+            self._copy_test_inputs(fixture)
+            self._make_git_fixture(fixture, layout)
+
+            if layout == "merge":
+                tracked = self._git(fixture, "show", "HEAD:docs/changelog.md")
+                stat = self._git(fixture, "show", "--stat", "HEAD")
+                self.assertIn(f"## {self.rcc_version}", tracked)
+                self.assertNotIn("docs/changelog.md", stat)
+            if layout == "untracked":
+                self.assertTrue((fixture / "docs" / "changelog.md").is_file())
+                self.assertEqual(self._git(fixture, "ls-files", "docs/changelog.md"), "")
+
+            output_dir = fixture / "robot-output"
+            result = subprocess.run(
+                [
+                    sys.executable,
+                    "-m",
+                    "robot",
+                    "--outputdir",
+                    str(output_dir),
+                    "robot_tests/development_process.robot",
+                ],
+                cwd=fixture,
+                capture_output=True,
+                text=True,
+            )
+
+            output_xml = output_dir / "output.xml"
+            self.assertTrue(output_xml.is_file(), f"Robot output missing: {result.stdout}\n{result.stderr}")
+            tests = list(ET.parse(output_xml).getroot().iter("test"))
+            self.assertEqual(len(tests), 1, result.stdout + result.stderr)
+            status = tests[0].find("status")
+            actual_passed = status is not None and status.get("status") == "PASS"
+            self.assertEqual(
+                actual_passed,
+                should_pass,
+                f"layout={layout}, exit={result.returncode}, XML={ET.tostring(tests[0], encoding='unicode')}, "
+                f"stdout={result.stdout!r}, stderr={result.stderr!r}",
+            )

+            self._git(fixture, "commit", "-m", "add prior-version changelog")
+            return
+        if layout == "normal":
+            self._write_changelog(fixture, self.rcc_version)
+            self._git(fixture, "add", "docs/changelog.md")
+            self._git(fixture, "commit", "-m", "add current changelog")

+            self._write_changelog(fixture, self.rcc_version)
+            self._git(fixture, "add", "docs/changelog.md")
+            self._git(fixture, "commit", "-m", "add current changelog")
+            self._git(fixture, "checkout", "-b", "feature")

+            (fixture / "mainline.txt").write_text("mainline change\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            self._git(fixture, "add", "mainline.txt")

+            self._git(fixture, "merge", "--no-ff", "feature", "-m", "merge feature")

+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+        )

+import os
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+from scripts import toc
+
+
+class TocOrderingTests(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_shuffled_glob_order_has_stable_output_and_keeps_priorities(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
+            root = Path(temporary)
+            docs = root / "docs"
+            docs.mkdir()
+            titles = {
+                "usecases.md": "Use cases",
+                "features.md": "Features",
+                "alpha.md": "Alpha",
+                "zeta.md": "Zeta",
+                "README.md": "Ignored README",
+                "toc.md": "Ignored TOC",
+                "changelog.md": "Ignored changelog",
+                "BUILD.md": "Ignored build notes",
+            }
+            for name, title in titles.items():
+                (docs / name).write_text(f"# {title}\n", encoding="utf-8")
+            for priority in toc.PRIORITY_LIST:
+                priority_path = docs / Path(priority).name
+                if not priority_path.exists():
+                    priority_path.write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
+
+            first_glob_order = [
+                "zeta.md", "features.md", "README.md", "alpha.md",
+                "usecases.md", "changelog.md", "BUILD.md", "toc.md",
+            ]
+            second_glob_order = list(reversed(first_glob_order))
+
+            def generate(names):
+                with mock.patch.object(
+                    toc.glob,
+                    "glob",
+                    return_value=[f"docs/{name}" for name in names],
+                ):
+                    previous = Path.cwd()
+                    try:
+                        os.chdir(root)
+                        toc.process()
+                        return (docs / "README.md").read_bytes()
+                    finally:
+                        os.chdir(previous)
+
+            first = generate(first_glob_order)
+            second = generate(second_glob_order)
+            self.assertEqual(first, second)
+            output = first.decode("utf-8")
+            self.assertLess(output.index("## 1 [Use cases]"), output.index("## 2 [Features]"))
+            self.assertLess(output.index("## 3 [Alpha]"), output.index("## 4 [Zeta]"))
+            for ignored_title in ("Ignored README", "Ignored TOC", "Ignored changelog", "Ignored build notes"):
+                self.assertNotIn(ignored_title, output)

## Outcome

Make RCC/Holotree the **authoritative environment engine** underneath local Action Server, distributed Action workers, bundles, offline delivery, and future providers.

The required experience is:

> Resolve/build an environment once, give it a portable cryptographic identity, publish it once when desired, hydrate it on any compatible worker, acquire it at API speed when warm, execute through a fresh bounded handle, and release it without making a local path or one shared filesystem lock the durable contract.

This is the foundation consumed by `joshyorko/actions#133`. It must preserve the best current RCC behavior:

- fully local use with one binary and no service;
- current `rcc run` / `rcc holotree variables` compatibility;
- deterministic environment blueprints and Holotree reuse;
- fast repeated execution;
- air-gapped export/import;
- enterprise endpoint and proxy controls;
- transparent Action Server reload when source changes without unnecessary environment rebuilds.

This issue is intentionally ambitious, but **v1 is evolutionary, not a rewrite**. The first implementation wraps and exposes the existing catalog/Hololib engine before replacing its storage or materialization internals.

## Product invariant

A durable environment is not:

- `CONDA_PREFIX`;
- `PYTHON_EXE`;
- a Holotree space name;
- one `RCC_HOME` / `ROBOCORP_HOME`;
- a mutable package directory;
- a process-local environment dictionary;
- an OCI tag;
- a server URL.

A durable environment is:

```text
canonical Environment Specification
            |
 cryptographic specification digest
            |
 platform + builder compatibility
            |
 verified Environment Artifact Manifest
            |
 catalog(s) + immutable content objects
            |
 worker-local materialization + lease
            |
 fresh execution handle
```

Local paths and activation variables are derived worker state. They may be returned to a caller, but they are never the portable identity.

## Non-negotiable local and reload UX

RCC is valuable because the normal path feels local and immediate. The distributed design must not make the local path worse.

### Local collapsed path

```text
Action/package request
        |
 local RCC environment resolve/acquire
        |
 active materialization or local Hololib restore
        |
 execution handle
        |
 Python process
```

No remote provider, daemon, container engine, Rails application, Kubernetes installation, or login is required.

### Source-only reload

Action source identity and environment identity are separate.

When Action Server or another runtime is in autoreload mode:

1. source changes are detected;
2. if the normalized Environment Specification is unchanged, RCC reuses the same verified materialization/lease class;
3. the runtime reloads/replaces the Action process generation without solver or package-network work;
4. the catalog/process surface updates without changing environment identity.

This preserves the current high-value workflow where an LLM can edit Actions while calls/runs remain visible and the server automatically reloads.

### Environment-changing reload

When dependency/environment inputs change:

1. resolve a new Environment Specification identity;
2. acquire a compatible published artifact or build one;
3. verify and materialize it beside the old generation;
4. keep in-flight Attempts on the old leased materialization;
5. atomically route new execution to the ready generation;
6. release/evict the old generation only after its users drain.

A source watcher must never make an in-flight execution silently switch environments.

## Current implementation archaeology

Any implementation agent must inspect the current code before changing it.

### Existing Holotree engine

Current `main` still uses:

- v12 platform-specific catalog names in `htfs/library.go`;
- a real filesystem stage followed by `Root.Lift`, relocation scanning, per-object Lift, catalog save, and publication;
- one compressed Hololib file per catalog digest;
- gzip `BestSpeed` for compressed Lift in `htfs/functions.go`;
- per-file Drop to a `.part` destination, decompression, digest verification, relocation rewrite, chmod, and rename;
- a broad filesystem lock around environment construction/recording in `htfs.RecordEnvironment`;
- local spaces as real writable filesystem trees.

That path is production-compatible and remains the v1 materializer.

### Current digest boundary

Current cache/catalog identity is not sufficient as a remote trust identity:

- modern file digests use fixed-key SipHash-128;
- `BlueprintHash` is a 64-bit SipHash-derived key;
- legacy content may use SHA-256.

These keys remain useful for existing catalog lookup and local compatibility. A hostile/shared remote CAS needs additional cryptographic identities. Do not silently rename a legacy key to `sha256`.

### Existing remote path

Current `rccremote` is a separate binary and a cache-export server:

- it requires shared Holotree mode;
- `/parts/<catalog>` returns a newline-separated set of legacy object IDs;
- `/delta/<catalog>` creates and serves a ZIP containing requested objects plus the catalog;
- the client writes that ZIP, takes the local Holotree lock, and imports it;
- pull configuration is largely `--origin`, `RCC_REMOTE_ORIGIN`, and `RCC_REMOTE_AUTH`;
- there is no first-class push, manifest commit, capability discovery, provider profile, resumable object publication, or remote retention contract.

Preserve read compatibility, but do not extend `/parts` and `/delta` into the permanent v2 API by accident.

### Existing bundle path

`rcc holotree build-from-bundle` can:

- read `envs/<name>/conda.yaml`;
- import an embedded `hololib/hololib.zip`;
- build or restore environments through existing Holotree APIs;
- read ordinary or appended ZIP payloads.

This is a useful carrier seed. It is not yet a common artifact format because identity and contents are encoded through ZIP path conventions instead of a versioned manifest/object index.

### Existing builders

- micromamba/conda-forge remains the broad compatibility builder;
- merged uv-native support can install a selected uv/Python path without conda channels and showed a useful cold-build improvement in its tested workload;
- builder choice is an implementation strategy behind the Environment Artifact contract;
- no builder strategy becomes portable identity merely because it produced `PYTHON_EXE`.

## Architectural decision

### Chosen v1 path

**Wrap the existing v12 catalogs and current Hololib object bytes in a cryptographically identified Environment Artifact Manifest.**

This deliberately separates two concerns:

```text
portable identity / publication / acquisition
                    |
        existing Holotree storage engine
```

The first vertical therefore does **not** require:

- a new catalog format;
- zstd;
- packfiles;
- FUSE;
- hardlinks/reflinks;
- OCI image execution;
- a central service;
- an RCC daemon.

Once the artifact/provider/materializer boundary exists, any of those internals may evolve behind compatibility tests.

### Why this order

It immediately unlocks the fleet-level win:

```text
cold build once
      |
cryptographic artifact publication
      |
N workers acquire + verify + restore
```

without first solving every local filesystem optimization.

It also prevents bundles, HTTP remote, object storage, OCI, and Action Runtime integration from inventing different environment identities.

## Environment Artifact Manifest v1

Exact Go types and canonical serialization require implementation review, but v1 must carry these semantics.

### Required identities

1. **Legacy blueprint key**
   - current `BlueprintHash`;
   - retained only for v12 lookup/compatibility.

2. **Environment Specification digest**
   - cryptographic digest of canonical normalized dependency/build inputs;
   - includes target platform/architecture and all policy that can change resolution/build semantics;
   - algorithm is explicit, initially `sha256`.

3. **Catalog digest**
   - cryptographic digest of the exact existing v12 catalog bytes;
   - legacy catalog name retained as metadata.

4. **Stored-object digest**
   - cryptographic digest of the exact stored Hololib object bytes transferred through a provider;
   - distinct from the legacy logical/catalog object ID;
   - includes byte size and storage encoding.

5. **Manifest digest / Artifact identity**
   - cryptographic digest of canonical manifest content excluding mutable signatures/locations as defined by the schema;
   - independent of tag, URL, bucket key, local path, and provider.

### Seed shape

```json
{
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.rcc.environment.manifest.v1+json",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "artifactDigest": "sha256:...",
  "specification": {
    "digest": "sha256:...",
    "legacyBlueprintKey": "...",
    "sourceKind": "package-yaml|conda-yaml|normalized-lock"
  },
  "platform": {
    "os": "linux",
    "arch": "amd64",
    "rccPlatform": "linux64"
  },
  "builder": {
    "kind": "micromamba-uv|uv-native|...",
    "rccVersion": "...",
    "compatibilityKey": "...",
    "inputsDigest": "sha256:..."
  },
  "catalogs": [
    {
      "legacyName": "...v12.linux64",
      "mediaType": "application/vnd.rcc.holotree.catalog.v12+gzip",
      "digest": "sha256:...",
      "size": 0
    }
  ],
  "objectIndex": {
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.rcc.holotree.object-index.v1+json",
    "digest": "sha256:...",
    "count": 0,
    "totalStoredBytes": 0,
    "totalLogicalBytes": 0
  },
  "provenance": {
    "createdAt": "...",
    "sourceDigest": "sha256:...",
    "sbomDigest": "sha256:..."
  },
  "requirements": {
    "catalogReaders": ["v12"],
    "features": ["gzip-objects", "relocation-v1"]
  }
}
```

The object index maps, at minimum:

```text
legacy catalog object ID
    -> cryptographic stored-byte digest
    -> stored size / logical size
    -> storage encoding
```

Do not duplicate the full catalog tree into the manifest. The existing catalog remains the reconstruction description; the manifest/index adds portable cryptographic and transport identity.

### Canonicalization requirements

- deterministic field ordering/encoding;
- no local timestamps or paths in identity-bearing fields unless deliberately normalized;
- explicit digest algorithms;
- unknown required feature causes fail-closed;
- optional metadata cannot silently change Artifact identity rules;
- signatures/attestations bind the manifest digest, not a mutable tag.

## Core Go seams

Do not start with CLI handlers. Establish narrow typed contracts.

### Builder / resolver

```go
type EnvironmentResolver interface {
    Resolve(ctx context.Context, input ResolveInput) (EnvironmentSpecification, error)
}

type EnvironmentBuilder interface {
    Build(ctx context.Context, spec EnvironmentSpecification) (BuiltEnvironment, error)
}
```

The existing micromamba and uv-native paths adapt behind this seam over time. V1 may initially wrap the current `ComposeFinalBlueprint` / `RecordEnvironment` path.

### Artifact assembler

```go
type ArtifactAssembler interface {
    FromExistingCatalog(ctx context.Context, catalog string) (ArtifactManifest, error)
}
```

It cryptographically inventories the existing catalog and referenced Hololib objects without rewriting them.

### Artifact provider

```go
type ArtifactProvider interface {
    Capabilities(ctx context.Context) (ProviderCapabilities, error)
    Resolve(ctx context.Context, ref ArtifactReference) (ArtifactManifest, error)
    MissingObjects(ctx context.Context, objects []StoredObject) ([]StoredObject, error)
    PutObject(ctx context.Context, object StoredObject, r io.Reader) error
    CommitManifest(ctx context.Context, manifest ArtifactManifest) error
    GetObject(ctx context.Context, object StoredObject) (io.ReadCloser, error)
}
```

Required semantics:

- object puts are idempotent by cryptographic digest;
- object bytes are verified before becoming visible as valid;
- `CommitManifest` is atomic and fails unless all required objects/catalogs/indexes exist and match;
- an existing digest-identical manifest makes commit idempotently successful;
- conflicting mutable publication cannot overwrite artifact identity;
- provider URL/tag is a reference, not identity;
- partial uploads remain unreachable and GC-eligible.

### Materializer

```go
type EnvironmentMaterializer interface {
    Acquire(ctx context.Context, manifest ArtifactManifest) (Materialization, error)
    Verify(ctx context.Context, materialization Materialization) error
    Lease(ctx context.Context, materialization Materialization, owner LeaseOwner) (Lease, error)
    ExecutionHandle(ctx context.Context, lease Lease) (ExecutionHandle, error)
    Release(ctx context.Context, lease Lease) error
}
```

V1 uses normal Holotree Drop/space materialization.

### Local store

Define local records for:

- known Artifact Manifests;
- verified catalog/index/object presence;
- materializations keyed by Artifact identity + local policy;
- leases;
- build/acquire state;
- last use and size;
- repair/GC state.

The exact persistence mechanism is open. Prefer the smallest atomic local implementation that supports independent RCC/worker processes. Do not create a network database requirement.

## Lock and concurrency redesign

The current broad environment-construction lock must not become fleet coordination.

V1 should move toward lock scopes such as:

1. **per build key**
   - specification + platform + builder compatibility;
   - prevents duplicate local build for the same result.

2. **per stored object**
   - atomic temp write + cryptographic verification + rename;
   - unrelated objects can arrive concurrently.

3. **per manifest/artifact commit**
   - verifies complete local state before publication.

4. **per materialization**
   - one process creates/repairs a space;
   - other processes wait/reuse after verification.

5. **short catalog/index mutation lock**
   - only where current shared indexes require serialization.

Unrelated environments must be able to build/acquire concurrently when filesystem/resource policy permits.

Distributed build single-flight is a separate optional provider/coordinator capability:

```text
build key claim -> owner/heartbeat/expiry -> verified publication
```

A remote claim never grants permission to publish incomplete state, and a local-only/offline build remains possible without a coordinator.

## Provider and `rccremote` v2

### Same binary, compatibility wrapper

The core server should be callable from the main RCC binary, for example:

```text

```

or an equivalent accepted name.

The existing `rccremote` binary may remain as a thin compatibility wrapper invoking the same package/API. Do not maintain two different protocol implementations.

### V2 protocol seed

Exact routes are open, but the protocol must provide these operations:

```text
GET  capabilities
GET  manifest by immutable digest/reference
POST missing-object negotiation
PUT  immutable object by cryptographic digest
PUT  immutable catalog/index object
POST atomic manifest commit
GET  immutable object with range/resume support where practical
```

The first provider may be a simple filesystem-backed HTTP implementation used by two local processes. That is enough to prove semantics.

- preserve existing `/parts`, `/delta`, and pull behavior during migration;
- allow a v1 catalog to be wrapped into a v2 Manifest;
- do not make new workers publish through the legacy protocol;
- produce explicit diagnostics when only legacy identity is available.

## Lease and GC model

An environment lease protects:

- the selected local materialization;
- required catalogs/indexes;
- required local content objects;
- any materializer-specific mount/overlay state.

Required behavior:

- independent local processes can acquire compatible leases;
- GC cannot remove leased state;
- release is idempotent;
- process/worker crash creates a recoverable stale lease;
- stale reconciliation uses PID plus process-start identity or another anti-PID-reuse mechanism where available;
- expiry alone must not delete files still used by a live foreign process;
- disk-pressure policy is explicit and observable;
- a remotely retained Artifact allows aggressive local eviction after release;
- immutable content is never modified in place for cleanup.

Environment leases are local resource protection. They are not distributed Action Run/Attempt fencing; `joshyorko/actions#83/#90/#133` own that authority.

## Performance doctrine

### First optimization: avoid repeated cold builds

The principal fleet optimization is:

```text
cold solve/build/Lift once
       |
publish complete artifact
       |
all later workers acquire/verify/Drop
```

Do not judge this architecture only by shaving milliseconds from local decompression.

### Phase 0 reproducible baseline

Before changing storage or Drop semantics, add/recover a benchmark harness pinned to current `main`.

Representative fixtures:

1. tiny pure-Python environment;
2. medium uv-native environment;
3. conda-heavy environment with compiled libraries;
4. many-small-file stress environment;
5. environment with relocation-heavy files.

Measure separately:

- specification normalization/hash;
- dependency resolution/build;
- Lift/relocation scan/catalog;
- artifact inventory/cryptographic hashing;
- publication negotiation/upload;
- remote download;
- verification/import;
- Drop/materialization;
- warm existing-materialization acquire;
- execution-handle derivation;
- Python startup and representative imports;
- source-only Action reload;
- environment-changing reload.

Capture:

- wall/CPU time;
- peak memory;
- bytes transferred/stored;
- object/file counts and size distribution;
- pprof profiles;
- syscall/file-operation counts where supported;
- platform and filesystem;
- cache-hit class.

Use Linux amd64 as the first implementation platform, then validate Windows and macOS arm64 before claiming cross-platform gains.

### Acceptance gates

- existing fully local workflows do not regress materially against current `main`;
- warm active-materialization acquire is API-speed and does no solver/network package work;
- local-Hololib acquisition is no slower than the current equivalent baseline unless justified by stronger verification;
- empty Worker B acquires a prebuilt remote Artifact without conda/PyPI/channel access;
- source-only reload performs no environment build/acquire beyond validating the existing identity;
- all performance claims include fixture, exact commit, command, platform, storage, run count, and raw output.

### Deferred storage/materializer experiments

#### zstd

Re-evaluate as a small isolated change after the baseline:

- dual-read compatibility;
- explicit new-write format/version;
- realistic whole-environment benchmarks;
- no bundled hardlinks, FUSE, prefetch, cache redesign, or release changes.

#### packfiles

Proceed only if current profiling shows source-object opens/metadata/syscalls are material.

- begin with small non-relocatable objects;
- maintain per-object logical identity plus cryptographic pack/index identity;
- retain crash-safe destination publication;
- do not remove `.part`/atomic behavior merely to improve a synthetic benchmark;
- test repair and partial pack corruption.

#### FUSE / virtual materializer

Treat as an optional Linux-first `EnvironmentMaterializer`, not the default artifact model.

It must prove:

- Python startup/import performance;
- relocation correctness;
- symlinks/modes;
- copy-on-write and `.pyc`;
- mount crash/recovery;
- lease integration;
- debug/inspection experience;
- fallback to ordinary Drop;
- dependency/install requirements.

#### OCI

OCI may provide:

- a manifest/object carrier;
- registry indexing/distribution;
- a self-contained container export containing RCC, source, and a prebuilt environment.

It does not define Environment Artifact identity and is not required for local/remote workers.

#### TUI

The TUI is deliberately last. It consumes the stable JSON/provider/cache APIs and must not define them.

## Security and trust

RCC/Holotree is reproducibility/content infrastructure, not a malicious-code sandbox.

Required:

- cryptographic remote identities even while legacy SipHash catalog keys remain;
- verify exact stored bytes, catalog bytes, object index, and manifest;
- fail closed on missing/unknown required features;
- reject traversal, unsafe symlinks, archive escapes, size bombs, and partial content;
- never share one writable live environment across mutually untrusted executions by default;
- preserve relocation semantics;
- signatures/attestations are optional policy inputs over immutable digest identity;
- knowing a digest does not grant authorization to read or execute it;
- no package secret/OAuth/data credential in Artifact content;
- provider auth and artifact trust are separate;
- added dependencies require license, maintenance, supply-chain, and cross-build review.

2. RCC constructs Manifest v1 + Object Index over the existing v12 catalog and Hololib bytes.
3. A publishes missing immutable objects and atomically commits the Manifest to a local HTTP provider.
4. Process B uses an empty `RCC_HOME`.
5. B resolves the immutable Artifact, downloads only missing bytes, verifies every cryptographic identity, imports/reuses the v12 catalog/content, and materializes a normal space.
6. B executes `python -c` importing representative dependencies without contacting conda, PyPI, uv releases, or package channels.
7. A second acquire on B reports a live/local cache hit and is fast enough for request-time use.
8. Source-only Action reload reuses the same Artifact identity and materialization.
9. Two publishers race; no partial or conflicting Manifest becomes authoritative.
10. One object is tampered with remotely and locally; acquisition fails closed and repair succeeds from valid content.
11. GC runs during an active lease; execution survives and the materialization becomes reclaimable after release.
12. Existing `rcc run`, `rcc holotree variables`, v12 export/import, and no-provider local use continue to work.

This vertical is a credible focused-day target for a strong agent/human pairing **only if scope stops here**. Remote production auth, resumable large uploads, provider GC, OCI, FUSE, packfiles, zstd migration, every platform, and full Action Runtime rollout are later gates—not honest same-day completion claims.

---

## Required invariants

- Portable identity is cryptographic and independent of local paths/provider locations.
- Legacy SipHash keys remain explicit compatibility metadata, never mislabeled as cryptographic trust.
- A Manifest is visible only after all referenced content is verified.
- A local materialization is disposable derived state.
- A worker can always rebuild/acquire the pinned Artifact after local cache loss.
- Active leases prevent local GC without becoming distributed Run ownership.
- No shared writable fleet-wide Holotree is required.
- Remote/provider failure does not break fully local operation when required content is local.
- Platform, catalog-reader, storage encoding, relocation, and builder compatibility are explicit.
- Old/new catalog/object formats may coexist behind readers.
- Source reload and environment replacement are generation-safe.
- Storage optimizations cannot weaken verification or cross-platform correctness by default.
- No agent-runtime, Kubernetes, container, Rails, or SaaS concept enters the core environment contract.

---

## Non-goals

- Building an agent harness, planner, model runtime, or conversation store.
- Replacing Action Run/Attempt fencing.
- Requiring RCC to become a daemon.
- Requiring Kubernetes, containers, OCI, NFS, Rails, Kamal, Cloudflare, or a central SaaS.
- Making one shared writable Hololib/space the fleet architecture.
- Treating RCC as a malicious-code sandbox.
- Default hardlinks/reflinks across untrusted writable executions.
- Removing integrity checks for speed.
- Reviving PR #64 or another old branch wholesale.
- Designing the TUI before stable machine APIs.
- Solving every builder and OS in the first vertical.
